title: [CRY2-3] Envelope `id` covers unsigned bytes, so any forwarder can change it, yet it decides Commit
description: Review finding CRY2-3: Envelope `id` covers unsigned bytes, so any forwarder can change it, yet it decides Commit races and message order (lens CRY2). Location: spec/05-messaging.md:28, 244, 248; spec/10-relays.md:756; spec/06-calls.md:495; spec/14-jmap.md:114. Fix: Confirmed. `powProof` is outside `signed` (10-relays.md:756), and any nonce that meets the difficulty is valid. A forwarder can also add an optional `powProof` that was not there. A relay can therefore grind variants of the same `signed` bytes to any desired `id` ordering without the admission key. Under the no-sequencer rule, a member that receives both an honest copy and a ground copy still picks the lowest `id`, so the attack works even when honest relays deliver promptly. "Relays MUST store and forward ... exactly as received" binds honest relays only. There is no deterministic-CBOR requirement for the outer map either. Fix: define `id` as the CIDv1 (raw, SHA2-256) of the `signed` byte string at 05:248. State that `powProof` and the outer encoding are not part of the identity, and change 05:244 and 10-relays.md:756 ("the envelope `id` covers it") to match. Relays still store the full envelope. Dedup, pinning, history and ordering all keep working, because only an admission-key holder can produce new `signed` bytes. Full text: notes/review2/CRY2-verified.md and notes/review2/CRY2.md.
